_about: Sprint 18 (s18-chop; Zafar, 7 Nov: chop as its own game, 'as other games and recipes will use chop'): the chop game's settings (js/cook/stations/chop.js reads this file; its own mechanic is js/cook/mechanics/chop.js, whose base knobs stay data/cook.json mechanics.chop until they move here). station: its name, verb, goal and phase line (the grown-ups' '?' box). view: its worktop (the white marble, the kitchen family's, STD-E3-03: the placeholder for the chop's board until ART-37 lands, decision 7). recipe: Nani's order (registered as Cook.Recipes.chop, the engine says it: STD-A4-01): DAAR-37's kinds and chops by level, a 'no' from L2 said last (DAAR-36). levels: what changes by level over the mechanic's knobs (phases: rounds with a switch; L4's speed about 15% over L3's, STD-C2-06). The decoys and the lookalike are the central rules' (data/rules.json levels), read in code, never here (STD-F2-02).

station.name: Chop
station.goal: Nani says what to chop and how many. Swipe the knife through only those, as many of each as she says. When the last one is chopped, the board is done. Listen: from level 2 she switches to the next thing while you chop.

phases.chop: Swipe the knife through what Nani names, as many as she says.

art._about: S19 (wave B; ART-37, CK-71): the chop's own pictures (the full art run's P1, P2 and K3, build/reports/s19-art-cuts.md): each piece whole (it sits in its slot on the band and hops) and in two clean halves (a cut lays half-a to the left and half-b to the right on the board, where they stay); the knife (kit/knife, blade up: blade gives its edge's two ends as fractions of the picture, tip then heel); the walnut board (samosa's v3, reused: the art plan's 'the v3 walnut board above the band'). Shadows are drawn in code. Loaded while Nani's order is read (CK-48), never before the chop is chosen (decision 68).

layout._about: S19 (wave B; ART-37: 'the board above the band (not full-bleed)'): every place in the 1600 x 900 design box, inside x 150-1450 (the narrowest play area, 1920x1080, shows that much: the stage fits by height). board: the walnut board's centre and height (its width from the picture: never stretched), as big as the room above the band allows; hopOn: the board's left and right that every hop's top keeps inside (the band's slots span the whole band, so its pills are wide enough to read; where they reach past the board, the hops go up and a little in); peak: an item's middle at the top of its hop (the board's middle); ring: the countdown ring left of the board; knife: where it rests, upright beside the board's right edge (px: its height); halves: how far a cut's two halves part (design px) and their size against the whole; shadow: the board's, items' and halves' soft shadow (offset x, y in design px, alpha, blur), down and to the right (one light, upper left).

recipe._about: DAAR-37 (Zafar, 30 Oct: 'Daar I meant 4 types of things to chop in the chop game - the number of total chops per play per level can go: 2, 4, 6, 8 (min 1 and max 3 chops per single item)'): kinds 1-4 by level (his 4 at L4; 1-3 below Claude's reading, to confirm at his play), chops 2, 4, 6, 8, each kind 1-3; garlic the fourth kind. One tomato at most (LNG-17: no Kutchi plural yet), so L1's one kind is never the tomato. 'rules': 'chop' reads data/rules.json count.games.chop (x the kinds, y the chops) once it is there; byLevel is the stand-in until then. A 'no' from L2 (the central rules' noAsks; CK-50 keeps L1 free of one), said last (DAAR-36). Kept out of free play (free: false).
recipe.how: Listen to what Nani wants chopped and how many, then swipe the knife through only those.
recipe._say: Each thing to chop is its own full sentence, 'Muke ba dungri khape.' (the engine's Need frame, as the pantry's GiveMe), so the card's any-order rows can be said in any order; a 'no' row 'Lasan na.' The board's own lines are the mechanic's ('Kali ba dungri. Ne hakro tameto.', the switch 'Hane trae mirchi!').

hop._about: S19 (CK-71; Zafar, 9 Nov: 'level 1 is just like only one item's flying in the air at a time ... you just have to catch it mid-flight. So you learn the mechanism'): the hop, the chop game's own (the mechanic's params.hop; daar's and chaat's chops never read it). up: the most items up on the board at once; rise, hang, fall: an item's hop in seconds (hang: how long it stays up to be swiped, at least 1.5 s at L1 for a 3-6 year old); every: the least time between two hops' starts (never less than (rise + hang + fall) / up); peak: the middle of an item at the top of its hop, design px (the board above the band); catchPad: the swipe's catch area, the item's whole picture plus this margin, design px; tapCuts: a tap on an item that is up chops it too (L1); decoys: the decoy kinds on the shelf (L1: none, his 9 Nov words; from L2 left out, so the central rules' count, data/rules.json); size, phoneSize: an item at the top of its hop, design px (phoneSize under 800 px wide); refill: seconds before a cut item's slot has a whole one again. jitter (Zafar, 9 Nov: 'random intervals or semi-random intervals ... nicely spaced out'): each gap between hop starts is every x (1 +/- jitter), drawn from the round's seed; minGap: never less than this many seconds between two starts, so two never set off together (and still never more than up at once). L1 stays one at a time, nearly steady.
L2 (his: 'level 2, there are 2 items. Sometimes one of them a decoy'): two up at once, the rules' two decoy kinds hopping as often as the one wanted.
L3: three up at once, quicker hops.

levels._about: L4: one kind a round (four rounds, three switches), a little quicker than L3 (STD-C2-06: throws 0.53 s apart against L3's 0.58, about 2.6 s in the air against 2.8), and one more spare throw of each wanted thing, since every round has four decoys

hop._about: L4: three up at once, quicker again (about 15% over L3, STD-C2-06), the rules' four decoys with a lookalike.

items._about: S19 (wave B): each piece's card picture is its own whole picture (the kit's cards read a game's items[].card for their word: js/cook/ui.js cardOfIds), so the order card shows exactly what sits on the band (contract-104).
